title: Axis rises above 200% when the shown values are mostly high
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. The Admin role holds every permission, including Reports. To use another role, first check Settings > Roles & Permissions > that role: the Reports permission must be on.
  2. Pick one workplace in the workplace selector at the right of the top bar (e.g. QA Testing).
  3. Use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. A technician whose only clocked work in the range is billed far above the time clocked. Seed it with these steps:
    • Settings > Staff: pick a clockable technician who has no other clocked time this month (e.g. a new staff member "ZZAUTOTEST Tech" with Clockable on, Active, enrolled in this workplace).
    • Customers > New Customer, enter a name (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST High Tech") and save.
    • Work Orders > New Work Order for that customer, add a labor line with labor hours 1.00 (e.g. price $250.00) and assign the technician to the line.
    • In a second browser sign in as that technician, clock in on the line and clock out after 15 minutes (0.25 hours). Sign out there.
    • Back as Admin: approve the line, complete the work order, click Review, then Finance > Create Invoice. This technician's efficiency for this month is 1.00 / 0.25 x 100 = 400%.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. On the Technician Efficiency tile, click View details.
  3. In the Technician filter, untick everyone except the seeded technician.
  4. Hover the technician's point and read its value.
  5. Read the top label of the left-hand axis.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Only one point is plotted and it reads about 400% (every shown value is above 200%, so the middle value is above 200%).
  • The axis is not capped at 200%: it rises to fit the value, with a top label at or above 400%, and the point is drawn in full, not clipped.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9581 (Story 9, Chart Behavior); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 9. Context note on the axis (Story 9). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, screenshots of the SV-8311 build captured 2026-09-28) board 06_TechEff_After, used for on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R2: “When one value is far above the rest — a value above 200% while the median of the values stays at or below 200% — the axis caps at 200% so the rest of the data stays readable. The median is taken over every plotted value on the chart, pooled across all of its drawn lines rather than computed per line, counting only points that have a value; where the number of points is even it is the mean of the two middle values. When the highest value on the chart is at or below 200% the axis simply fits the data and no cap applies.”
  • Context note (Story 9, the axis): “the axis fits the data. It only pins to 200% when a single outlier would otherwise flatten the rest of the chart; when the data as a whole is genuinely high, the axis scales up to fit it. This behavior applies wherever the chart appears — inside an expanded tile and embedded on a report page (Story 11).”
